title: Queued-packet pile overlaps to one dot per lane — the serialization visual shows no queue depth
evidence: view.odin draw_packets: "frac := f32(pp.packet_progress_frac(p, bandwidth)) / 256.0" ... "pos = {depart.x + dx * frac, depart.y + dy * frac}" then the lateral offset "pos.x += (-by / blen) * bands.centers[lane] * width". A queued packet has progress_units == 0 (forward pass: "p.progress_units = 0"), so frac == 0 and every same-lane packet queued at the same node renders at the IDENTICAL pixel (depart node + band center). Verified against the blessed goldens: md5(goldens/qos_contention/01000ms.png) == md5(goldens/qos_contention/10000ms.png) == ebce0e7d9a9d317455b13e2d21f2595c (byte-identical captures), and pixel scans show only ~124 email px + ~52 streaming px total (≈4-5 dot-equivalents) at the captures, while a re-sim of the demo shows 13-14 in-flight packets at those ticks (~12 of them queued at progress 0 across the lane queues).
detail: The story's headline visual ('packets visibly queue and exit in lane order') collapses: a 6-deep lane queue renders as a single dot, so the contention demo shows lane order (3 piles) but no queue depth — the launchable's queue readout is invisible.
recommended_fix: Stagger queued packets deterministically within their lane (e.g., a small array-index-based micro-offset along the edge) so the pile shows depth; T2 goldens for qos_contention must re-bless.
